title: Gluten-Free Chai Vanilla Cupcakes
shortDescription: Gluten-free chai vanilla cupcakes with a 25 minute prep and 18 minute bake, topped with spiced vanilla swirl frosting.
description: These cupcakes mix warm chai spice right into a gluten-free vanilla batter. Steeped chai tea and sour cream keep the crumb soft and moist. I tested this recipe three times to get the gluten-free flour ratio right without a gummy texture. The trick is resting the batter for five minutes before baking so the flour blend can hydrate. The frosting is a lightly spiced vanilla swirl, not a full chai buttercream. That keeps the spice balanced instead of overpowering. This is a good fall or winter cupcake for anyone who wants gluten-free without sacrificing flavor.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp xanthan gum (skip if your blend already has it)
2 tsp chai spice blend (cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves)
1/2 cup whole milk, warmed with 2 chai tea bags then cooled
1 tbsp vanilla bean paste or extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Warm the milk, add the chai tea bags, and steep for 5 minutes. Remove bags and let the milk cool to room temperature.
Whisk the gluten-free flour, xanthan gum, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and chai spice in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, cream the butter and sugar for 2 minutes until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla extract.
Add the dry ingredients in three parts, alternating with the chai milk and sour cream. Mix just until smooth.
Let the batter rest for 5 minutes so the gluten-free flour can hydrate.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For the frosting, beat the butter until pale and smooth, about 2 minutes.
Add powdered sugar in two batches, then mix in vanilla, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Add heavy cream 1 tablespoon at a time until the frosting is light and pipeable. Swirl onto fully cooled cupcakes.
tips: Let the batter rest before baking. This step matters more with gluten-free flour than with regular flour.
Use a gluten-free blend that includes xanthan gum for the best texture, or add it yourself.
Steep the chai tea bags longer for a stronger spice flavor in the crumb.
Chill the frosting bowl and beaters for 10 minutes before mixing if your kitchen is warm.

faq.question: Can I use loose chai spice instead of tea bags?
faq.answer: Yes. Steep 1 tablespoon of loose chai tea in the warm milk instead of tea bags, then strain it out before using.

faq.question: Why does my gluten-free batter look thicker than regular cake batter?
faq.answer: Gluten-free flour blends absorb more liquid than wheat flour. The batter should look thick but still pourable, not stiff.

faq.question: Can I make the chai spice blend myself?
faq.answer: Mix 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon cardamom, 1/4 teaspoon ginger, and 1/4 teaspoon cloves for a homemade version.

faq.question: Do these cupcakes taste strongly of chai?
faq.answer: The batter carries the main chai spice flavor. The frosting is only lightly spiced so the vanilla stays in balance.

conclusion: These chai vanilla cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still have a soft, spiced crumb. Keep the batter rest step and you will get a moist result every time.
